items.title: Section: The Truth of Origin — Craving as Cause, Accumulation, Arising, and Condition

items.zh: 謂了知愛能引苦故，說名為因。既引苦已，復能招集令其生故，說名為集。既生苦已，令彼起故，說名為起。復於當來諸苦種子能攝受故，次第招引諸苦集故，說名為緣。
items.en: Knowing that craving is able to bring about suffering, it is called the cause. Having brought suffering about, craving is further able to accumulate it, causing it to arise, so it is called accumulation. Having given rise to suffering, craving causes it to actually manifest, so it is called arising. And since craving is further able to take hold of future seeds of suffering, drawing them in sequence into an accumulating mass of suffering, it is called condition.

items.zh: 復有差別。謂了知愛是取因故，復能招集即以其取為因有故，復能生起有為上首當來生故，又能引發以生為緣老、病、死等諸苦法故。隨其所應，當知說名因、集、起、緣。
items.en: There is a further distinction. Knowing that craving is the cause of grasping, it is called cause; being further able to accumulate the state of existence that has grasping as its cause, it is called accumulation; being further able to give rise to the future rebirth headed by that state of existence, it is called arising; and being further able to bring about the various sufferings of ageing, sickness, and death that take rebirth as their condition, it is called condition — each, as appropriate, understood by this same fourfold naming.

items.title: A Third Lens on Craving, and the Truth of Origin Complete

items.zh: 謂正了知煩惱隨眠附屬所依，愛隨眠等是當來世後有生因。又正了知彼所生纏，隨其所應，是集、起、緣。謂後有愛能招引故，即是其集；此後有愛，復能發起喜貪俱行愛；此喜貪俱行愛，復與多種彼彼喜愛為緣。
items.en: One correctly knows that the dormant afflictions are attached to their underlying basis, and that dormant craving and the like are the cause of a future existence yet to come … because this craving for a future existence is able to draw it forth, this itself is the accumulation; this craving for a future existence is further able to give rise to a joy-and-greed-linked craving; and this joy-and-greed-linked craving is further a condition for manifold instances of craving towards this and that pleasant thing.

items.zh: 如是依止愛隨眠等及三種纏，能生後有，及能發起諸愛差別，是故說名因、集、起、緣。如是行者，由四種行了集諦相。於集諦相正覺了已，

items.title: Section: The Truth of Cessation — Extinguished, Still, Sublime, and Free

items.zh: 復正覺了如是集諦無餘息滅，故名為滅。一切苦諦無餘寂靜，故名為靜。即此滅、靜，是第一故、是最勝故、是無上故、說名為妙。是常住故、永出離故，說名為離。
items.en: One further correctly comes to know that this very truth of origin is extinguished without remainder — this is called extinction … every aspect of the truth of suffering is stilled without remainder — this is called stillness … this very extinction and stillness is foremost, is most excellent, is unsurpassed — this is called sublime … it is permanent, and a final departure — this is called freedom.

items.zh: 如是行者，由四種行了滅諦相。於滅諦相正覺了已，

items.title: Section: The Truth of the Path — All Sixteen Aspects of the Four Truths Now Complete

items.zh: 復正覺了真對治道，於所知境能通尋求義故，能實尋求義故，由於四門隨轉義故，一向能趣涅槃義故，所以說名道、如、行、出。
items.en: One further correctly comes to know the genuine counteracting path: because, with respect to the objects to be known, it is able to lead through to what is sought, it is called the path; because it is able to genuinely reach what is sought, it is called the fitting way; because it operates by circulating through these four gateways, it is called the practice; and because it leads uniformly towards nirvāṇa, it is called the exit.

items.zh: 如是行者，由四種行了道諦相。如是名為於四聖諦自內現觀了相作意。

items.title: Section: Extending the Same Sixteen Aspects to What Cannot Be Directly Seen — Direct Knowledge and Analogical Knowledge

items.zh: 彼既如是於其自內現見諸蘊，依諸諦理，無倒尋思正觀察已。復於所餘不同分界不現見蘊，比度觀察。謂彼所有，有為、有漏，遍一切處、遍一切種，於一切時，皆有如是法、皆墮如是理、皆有如是性。彼所有滅，皆永寂靜，常住安樂。彼所有道，皆能永斷，究竟出離。
items.en: Having thus, with respect to one's own directly observed aggregates, correctly and without distortion investigated and observed according to the principle of the truths, one then, with respect to the remaining aggregates of a different, not-directly-observed realm, observes by inference instead … their cessation is entirely and permanently still, abiding in lasting bliss; and their path is entirely able to bring about permanent severance, ultimate departure.

items.zh: 當知此中，若於現見諸蘊諦智，若於所餘不同分界不現見境比度諦智，即是能生法智、類智種子依處。
items.en: One should know that, in this regard, the truth-wisdom concerning directly observed aggregates, and the truth-wisdom arrived at by inference concerning the remaining, not-directly-observed realm, are respectively the basis giving rise to the seeds of direct knowledge and of analogical knowledge.

items.zh: 又即如是了相作意，當知猶為聞思間雜。若觀行者，於諸諦中，如是數數正觀察故，由十六行，於四聖諦證成道理已得決定。復於諸諦盡所有性、如所有性，超過聞思間雜作意，一向發起修行勝解，此則名為勝解作意。如是作意，唯緣諦境，一向在定。於此修習、多修習故，於苦、集二諦境中，得無邊際智。由此智故，了知無常，發起無常無邊際勝解。如是了知苦等，發起苦無邊際勝解、空無我無邊際勝解、惡行無邊際勝解、往惡趣無邊際勝解、興衰無邊際勝解，及老病死愁悲憂苦一切擾惱無邊際勝解。此中無邊際者，謂生死流轉。如是諸法無邊無際，乃至生死流轉不絕，常有如是所說諸法。唯有生死無餘息滅，此可息滅，更無有餘息滅方便。

blocks.text: The other three truths, each with four aspects, making the classic sixteen. A short passage (0475a05) is untranslated.

"Knowing that craving is able to bring about suffering, it is called the **cause**; having brought it about, craving accumulates it: **accumulation**; it makes suffering actually arise: **arising**; it is the condition for its continuing: **condition**." The treatise gives three lenses on this, ending with dormant craving as the cause of future existence.

"This truth of origin is extinguished without remainder: **extinction**. Every aspect of suffering is stilled: **stillness**. This extinction is foremost, most excellent: **sublime**. It is permanent, a final departure: **freedom**."

"Because it leads through to what is sought: the **path**. Because it genuinely reaches it: the **fitting way** (如). Because it is practice: **practice** (行). Because it leads out: **departure** (出)."

Having investigated one's own, directly seen aggregates, one extends the sixteen aspects by inference to other realms not seen. These become "the seeds of direct knowledge and of analogical knowledge" (法智、類智).

All this is still "learning the mark", mixed with hearing and reflection. When certainty is gained, one goes beyond it to **confident understanding**, purely in concentration, with "boundless understanding" of impermanence, suffering, non-self, wrongdoing, bad destinies, rise and decline, and the endless troubles of ageing and death, throughout saṃsāra; "only saṃsāra's complete cessation can still them".

quiz.q: "Knowing that craving brings about suffering, it is called the cause." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: all craving is suffering — craving causes the fruit of suffering
quiz.why: "Knowing that craving is able to bring about suffering, it is called the cause." Master Cháng Bǎi: wherever there's craving there's suffering; craving is the cause producing the fruit of suffering.

quiz.q: "Further able to accumulate it, causing it to arise — accumulation." What image does Master Cháng Bǎi use?
options: the water of craving fertilizes suffering — moistening its seeds to sprout
quiz.why: "Having brought suffering about, craving is further able to accumulate it, causing it to arise, so it is called accumulation." Master Cháng Bǎi: the water of craving is good fertilizer for suffering; it keeps moistening suffering's seeds so they root and sprout — that's accumulation.

quiz.q: "The truth of origin extinguished without remainder — extinction." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: all afflictions — seeds and manifestations — wholly extinguished
quiz.why: "One further correctly comes to know that this very truth of origin is extinguished without remainder — this is called extinction." Venerable Miào Jìng: all afflictions, their seeds and their manifestations, are wholly extinguished — that's called extinction.

quiz.q: "Permanent, a final departure — freedom." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain?
options: permanently free of affliction, karma, and suffering
quiz.why: "It is permanent, and a final departure — this is called freedom." Venerable Miào Jìng: one has permanently left affliction, karma, and suffering — hence "freedom."

quiz.q: The path's "如," rendered "the fitting way." How do the masters explain?
options: Miào Jìng: through non-self one reaches the suchness of things — their quiescence; Cháng Bǎi: genuinely reaching cessation, in accord with suchness
quiz.why: "Because it is able to genuinely reach what is sought, it is called the fitting way." Venerable Miào Jìng: through the meaning of non-self one reaches the suchness of things — the quiescence of all phenomena. Master Cháng Bǎi: when the noble path succeeds, one can truly reach cessation, in accord with suchness. "Fitting way" doesn't bring out suchness.

quiz.q: "The remaining aggregates of a different, not-directly-observed realm." What is the "different realm," per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: unlike our desire-world — the form and formless realms
quiz.why: "One then, with respect to the remaining aggregates of a different, not-directly-observed realm, observes by inference instead." Venerable Miào Jìng: a world unlike ours with desire — the form and formless realms.

quiz.q: At this stage the truth-wisdom is only the "basis for the seeds." What is the practitioner, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
quiz.why: "Are respectively the basis giving rise to the seeds of direct knowledge and of analogical knowledge." Venerable Miào Jìng: so at this time he is still an ordinary person, not a noble one.
